newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's WAMCO cocoa butter output set to rise.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's WAMCO cocoa butter output set to rise.

text.p: Ghanaian cocoa butter producer West African Mills Company Ltd (WAMCO) expects production to rise by 20 percent in 1997 following a factory overhaul, its company director said on Friday.
"We started rehabilitation on the TAKSI cocoa processing plant, renamed WAMCO 2, in September 1995," company director Jelle Kuiper told Reuters.
WAMCO 2 would produce 24,000 tonnes in 1997 against 20,000 last year and 16,000 in 1995, said Kuiper.
The WAMCO 2 plant overhaul would be completed by mid-1997 after a total investment of 40 million marks, Kuiper added.
In 1992, German owner, Hosta, through its subsidiary Walter Shroeder, bought a 60 percent share in WAMCO, now WAMCO 1, with Ghana holding the other 40 percent.
Shroeder spent 20 million marks on refits before re-opening the plant in 1994.
In 1993, Schroeder bought a 60 percent stake in TAKSI, a Takoradi cocoa processing plant.
